regeln: Verify all spoken claims against source documentation and pair them with genuine tool UI, official documentation excerpts, or terminal outputs directly matching narration.
Replace text graphics, title slides, generic warning symbols, and stock footage with real software interface views, command-line recordings, or documentation screenshots.
Use precise technical diagrams or system schematics for abstract technical concepts instead of generic office workers or bulleted text cards.
Demonstrate specific actions like file operations or command executions using direct UI recordings or realistic mockups rather than simple visual metaphors.
Link technical capabilities to a concrete visual workflow or practical human task instead of listing specifications or version details.
Eliminate conversational script filler to ensure every line delivers factual substance, concrete detail, or visual clarity.
Display main visual elements prominently, avoiding empty vertical framing, tiny repeated photos, or unrelated background stock fillers.
Include mandatory spoken calls-to-action alongside matching visual interaction symbols or the channel presenter at format-appropriate timestamps.
Respect format-specific pacing without forcing Shorts cadence onto long videos or long-video structures onto Shorts.
Maintain continuous narration aligned with tightly timed subtitles, avoiding unrelated decorative backgrounds or filler clips.
Treat quality feedback as provisional data to build consistent general writing and clip-selection habits.
